授業科目の概要.授業科目に関する特筆事項: Ceramic proton-conducting membranes are essential materials for energy conversion. They exhibit high proton (hydrogen ion) conductivity at moderate temperatures, typically between 300 and 600 °C. In addition to their well-known functions in energy conversion and hydrogen production, these membranes facilitate proton-mediated electrochemistry at these temperatures. This capability opens up new opportunities to improve various electrochemical and thermochemical processes.  Given this potential, significant efforts have been devoted to advancing a variety of energy-related applications using these materials. This course covers recent advances in proton-conducting materials. It will begin with a fundamental overview, followed by a discussion of the fabrication and processing technologies essential to this area. Building on these advancements, the lectures will also explore emerging devices that utilize proton-conducting materials, including protonic ceramic fuel cells, electrolysis cells, and catalytic membrane reactors. Although many of these concepts are still in the early stages of development, they highlight the significant potential of protonic ceramics in integrating renewable energy with chemical manufacturing. The course combines theoretical concepts with practical applications to prepare students for cutting-edge research and industry advancements.

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）: 本講義は、学生にプロトン性セラミック材料の深い理解と、それらが持続可能なエネルギーソリューションにおいて果たす役割を理解させることを目指しています。
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）: This course aims to provide students with a deep understanding of protonic ceramic materials and their role in sustainable energy solutions. Provide a rigorous foundation in the crystal chemistry, defect chemistry, and proton-transport mechanisms of ceramic proton-conducting materials. Introduce the design principles and performance-limiting mechanisms of protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs), electrolysis cells (PCECs), and catalytic membrane reactors. Cultivate the ability to critically evaluate current research literature and identify open scientific and engineering challenges in this rapidly developing field. Prepare students to contribute to cutting-edge research and industrial innovation integrating renewable energy with chemical manufacturing.
